title: Canonical right derivation preserves an exact adjoint forgetting square
statement: Let $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $L_0:\mathcal C_0\to\mathcal D_0$ be exact additive left adjoints, with right adjoints $R,R_0$, between abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and K-injective total right derived functors [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]; assume K-injective resolutions in $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal D_0$. Let $U:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C_0$ and $V:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D_0$ be exact additive functors, with $V$ preserving K-injective complexes. Suppose $a:LV\cong UL_0$ and $b:RU\cong VR_0$ are specified isomorphisms, and $b$ is the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of $a^{-1}$. Then the mate of the exact localization $D(a)^{-1}$, using the specified adjunctions $D(L)\dashv RR$ and $D(L_0)\dashv RR_0$, is precisely the canonical isomorphism $RR\,D(U)\cong R(RU)\cong R(VR_0)\cong RV\,RR_0\cong D(V)\,RR_0$, where the composition isomorphisms are normalized by the right-derived units.

proof.text: Let beta be the displayed four-factor comparison. Expand the two rightDerivedUnique comparisons and rightDerivedFunctorNatIso. Their defining rightDerivedNatTrans_app equations give hcomp: the exact-postcomposition unit followed by beta equals the localized b followed by the V,R0 composite unit and the exact comparison for V. Evaluate it on a homotopy complex, cancel the identity composition isomorphisms, and use rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory_hom_fac for V. This proves the normalized comparison equation hbeta, with all exact-localization factors explicit. The source canonical K-injective constructions and these factorization equations are already proved; no separate existence theorem is used.

Apply Mathlib Adjunction.derivedη_fac_app to the homotopy adjunctions underlying the two specified canonical derived adjunctions. This gives heta and heta0. Lift the unit identity of the ordinary mate in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] to the homotopy category by quotient_obj_surjective and degreewise equality; hb identifies its right square with b. This is hc. The existing mapDerivedCategorySquareIso_hom_app_Qh_obj equation for a, together with a.hom_inv_id, gives the inverse-localization equation haDi for D(a).inv.

For a homotopy complex X, expand the first derived unit using heta. Naturality of beta moves the inverse L-localization factor to the far right. Naturality of the U-localization factor, followed by hbeta, rewrites the middle composite through Qh of the ordinary unit and b. Use hc, naturality of the R0-derived unit, heta0 and naturality of the second derived adjunction unit. The resulting composite equals the second unit followed by RR0 of D(a).inv, by haDi. This proves hq on every Qh X. Localization.natTrans_ext extends hq to all derived objects, giving hu. Only localization extensionality is used, not faithfulness of localization.

Expand the mate of D(a).inv componentwise. The first two factors are the right side of hu at RR(N), so replace them by U of the first derived unit followed by beta at D(L)(RR(N)). Naturality of beta at the derived counit moves that counit to U of RR. The right triangle identity cancels the resulting unit-counit composite, leaving beta at N. NatTrans.ext proves the asserted equality. No cancellation of a noninvertible derived unit, no assumption of K-injective resolutions in C0 and no new auxiliary sorry are used.
